title: Israel allows a limited quantity of food and medicine into Gaza after a near-total import ban
body:
On 19 May 2025, Israel began allowing a small amount of food and medicine into Gaza after a near-total ban on imports that it had imposed on 2 March 2025, according to an Associated Press report. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had eased the blockade under pressure from unnamed allies, and that the measure would bridge the gap until a new aid distribution system began operating.

The United Nations said only five trucks entered Gaza on the Monday, compared with about 600 per day during the earlier ceasefire. UN agencies and aid groups welcomed the move but said the quantity was nowhere near what was needed, and the World Food Programme said no food had yet reached the population. The UN said aid was stockpiled outside Gaza and could be distributed quickly if Israel permitted it. The United Kingdom, France and Canada called the aid wholly inadequate and threatened concrete actions, including sanctions.

The article cited Integrated Food Security Phase Classification figures indicating that nearly half a million Palestinians faced possible starvation and a further one million could barely get enough food. UNICEF said more than 9,000 children had been treated for malnutrition so far that year, and the UN Population Fund said up to 20 percent of Gaza's estimated 55,000 pregnant women were malnourished. The Hamas-run Gaza Health Ministry said more than 53,000 Palestinians had been killed. The new US-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation planned four distribution sites guarded by private security firms, which UN agencies and aid groups refused to join.
